title: TREASURE – Tenecteplase before interhospital transfer for thrombectomy (4.5–24h anterior LVO)

background.text: MAP agreed with the TREASURE study proposal and raised 5 follow-up suggestions covering transferring time distribution, power/interim analysis, drop-out rate, budget feasibility, and RA confirmation on IIS for registration.
background.quote:
MAP agrees with the study proposal, with the following suggestions.
Study design
1.Include distribution of transferring time in the results analysis.
2.Work with statisticians to assess the study power reduction and the scenarios of interim analysis
3.Re-evaluate the drop-out rate, leveraging ORIGINAL study results
4.Confirm the feasibility of current total budget proposal with PI
5.Confirm with RA regarding the current regulation on leveraging IIS study results for registration.

background.text: Feedback on all 5 MAP suggestions: (1) transferring time distribution included in TREASURE; (2) power updated to 0.85, interim analysis not recommended by PI or BDS; drop-out rate updated from 10% to 5% (ORIGINAL early discontinuation 4.4%); sample size reduced from 706 to 572 with ≥1:1 hospital fund matching confirmed; RA confirmed IIS cannot directly support registration.
background.quote:
Study power has been updated from 0.9 to 0.85. Interim analysis is not recommended from neither PI or BDS.
Drop out rate has been updated from 10% to 5%. (early discontinuation rate of 4.4% in the ORIGINAL).
Sample size has been reduced from 706 to 572. The study team has confirmed at least a 1:1 matching of funds from the hospital, and the current budget is feasible.
Confirmed with RA, these IIS cannot directly support the registration.

background.text: Power scenarios: observed case N=544 power 85.5% min cOR 1.345; imputed case N=572 power 86.8% min cOR 1.340.
background.quote: Scenario: Imputed case | N: 572 | Power: 86.8% | Min. detectable cOR: 1.340

background.text: Futility interim not recommended: less uncertainty on treatment effect, small sample size reduces reliability, investigator does not accept early stop; DMC recommended for safety and efficacy evaluation.
background.quote:
Futility interim is not recommended
There is less uncertainty on the treatment effect.
Small sample size result in low reliability.
Efficacy Interim benefits less
The investigator doesn’t accept early stop at interim considering low reliability result and potential challenge from reviewer.
DMC is recommended for safety and efficacy evaluation

title: ANGEL-MeVO-TNK – Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute primary medium vessel occlusion stroke

background.text: MAP agreed with the ANGEL-MeVO-TNK study proposal and raised 3 suggestions: re-evaluate drop-out rate using ORIGINAL results, assess timing of interim analysis, and check Tiantan Hospital registry for MeVO patients treated with IAT for more accurate treatment effect.
background.quote:
MAP agrees with the study proposal, with the following suggestions.
Study design
1.Re-evaluate the drop-out rate, leveraging ORIGINAL study results
2.Assess the timing of interim analysis, ensuring a balance between the data amount for IA and the remaining study duration
3.Check the registry study database from Tiantan Hospital regarding the condition of patients with MevO treated with IAT, for a more accurate treatment effect proposal

background.text: Feedback: drop-out rate maintained at 5% (ORIGINAL 4.4%); interim analysis not recommended by PI or BDS; treatment effect kept at 13% based on PI clinical assumption; no available Tiantan Hospital database for IA efficacy in MeVO, but IA with rtPA/TNK in anti-bridging LVO and IA with Urokinase in M1/M2 occlusions referenced.
background.quote:
Drop-out rate maintain 5% (early discontinuation rate of 4.4% in ORIGINAL study).
Interim analysis is not recommended from neither PI or BDS..
Treatment effect keep as 13% based on PI’s clinical assumption (No available database from Tiantan Hospital to evaluate the efficacy of IA in Mevo. While the efficacy of IA with rtPA/TNK in anti-bridging in LVO and IA with Urokinase in M1/M2 occlusions could be referred.)
